scope: Make low-level UNDERLAY serialization honor the configured resolver for its AcDbUnderlayDefinition reference.

issue.before: writeUnderlay always used remapObjectHandle for definitionHandle, bypassing the final-ID contract of setReferenceResolver.
issue.impact: A selected caller mapping could be ignored and the output reference could name the source/remapped object instead of the caller-selected definition identity.

behavior: The writer uses the resolver result as the final group-340 identity when a resolver is configured.
Without a resolver, the writer uses the established source-handle remap fallback.
Existing zero, NoHandle, and fixed-output-handle refusal remains in place before record emission.
The concrete adapter graph gate remains responsible for proving the target exists and has the correct definition kind.

validationProfile.source: Locally constructed in-memory PDFUNDERLAY record; no DWG/DXF fixture files.
cases: reference-resolver final identity overrides the configured remap

validation.focusedTestResult: PASS: 1/1; both ASCII/Binary x resolver/remap cases, 0.48 seconds

limitations: Generated low-level reference translation only; it does not prove target existence, target kind, owner role, graph closure, physical producer coverage, or native underlay display behavior.
P4 graph admission and P8 native consumer qualification remain open; no support claim is promoted.
next: Continue source-bound UNDERLAY definition/output binding checks and native Linux/Windows consumer qualification.
